newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech NPF sets Vitkovice, Nova Hut steel tenders.
newsitem.headline: Czech NPF sets Vitkovice, Nova Hut steel tenders.

text.p: The Czech privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), on Friday set two tenders for stakes of roughly 18.3 percent in both the Nova Hut and Vitkovice steelworks, an NPF statement said.
It said detailed bids should arrive at the headquarters of the NPF on December 12 between 0900 and 1200 local time (0800-1100 gmt).
Participation in the tenders is not limited, but "priority will be given to participants who display practical experience in similar transactions."
Bids must include information on the background of participants, an offer for the method of completing the transaction which conforms to Czech law, and a schedule for completion of the sale.
It also must detail planned methods of cooperation between the participant, the NPF, and the company, and planned methods and amounts of remuneration for managers of the steel company.
The bids will be reviewed until January 10, 1997 and results will be presented to participants in written form.
The NPF said further detailed rules for the tender were available at the NPF by calling (+42-2) 2499 1382.

The tenders are part of a broader privatisation plan for the two steelworks approved by the government in September, which called for putting the NPF shares on the market and giving a one percent stake to management with options.
The mills' management would get a five-year option to get a further 10 percent stake, which could only be executed if they succeed with their restructuring plans for the companies.
The government said criteria for the increased management stake included transparency of ownership, cooperation with local authorities, and increasing the firms' market value.
Vitkovice opened on Friday on the Prague Stock Exchange eight crowns higher at 220 crowns, but below its year-high of 336 crowns.
Nova Hut shares opened 11 crowns lower on the PSE at 369 crowns well below its year-high of 614 but above its year low of 249.
